modernClarificationFindings.judgment: Index-based optical density is the relevant comparison for Snell refraction; mass density is not substituted. Both prose locales expressly make this distinction.

Snell's non-divided n sin(alpha)=sin(beta) remains meaningful at zero; division by sin(beta) does not. For 0<alpha<=alpha_0 and n>1, beta>alpha within the real-ray angular domain. Both locales use the same domain and normal-angle convention.

The observation is localized near critical incidence, with explicit rejection of a universal polarization/interval monotonicity claim. In the ordinary lossless planar-interface model the transmitted normal energy flux tends to zero as beta tends to 90 degrees, and energy conservation makes reflectance tend to one. This does not turn visual brightness into a calibrated energy measurement.

Original inclusive wording is attributed, not changed in the snapshot. Critical equality is the grazing limit; for alpha>alpha_0, tangential wave number exceeds the propagating second-medium wave number, so its normal component is imaginary rather than an additional real refracted ray. Thus absence of a propagating beam need not mean absence of an evanescent electromagnetic field. No evanescent-field magnitude is asserted.

Source index/angle examples are explicitly attributed as approximate and rounded. Independent inverse-sine-relation arithmetic below demonstrates rounding compatibility, not recovery of an exact material constant, wavelength or source calculation. No source angle is replaced.

The usual higher-index-core/lower-index-cladding structure satisfies the dense-to-less-dense TIR condition. Local incidence remains important on bends, so arbitrary tight bends are not guaranteed to guide. This is explicitly modern explanation, not a purported literal source quote.

Corresponding input/output fiber positions are necessary for direct reconstruction from individually transported image elements, not for every encoded communication application. The original medical use and unwanted local bulb heat are retained without new efficacy or universal thermal claims.
